definition: Consumer reporting agency (CRA): a firm that compiles consumer credit files and sells reports to third parties, e.g. Equifax, Experian, TransUnion (FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681a(f)).
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. is where the Fair Credit Reporting Act is codified; complaint templates cite its subsections.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: FCRA 611 (15 U.S.C. 1681i): when a consumer disputes an item, the CRA must reinvestigate it, generally within 30 days, and correct or delete what it cannot verify.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: The usual FCRA reinvestigation deadline; also the FDCPA window for a consumer to dispute a debt after the collector's validation notice.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A payment reported to the bureaus as 30+ days past due; a negative tradeline entry that can stay on a report for up to seven years.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: The lender or account holder the debt is owed to (the original creditor), as distinct from a collector or debt buyer.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: 15 U.S.C. 1666b (Truth in Lending Act): a card issuer may not treat a payment as late unless the statement was mailed or delivered at least 21 days before the due date.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Furnisher duties under FCRA 623 (15 U.S.C. 1681s-2): lenders that report to bureaus must report accurately and investigate disputes forwarded by a CRA.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: An obligation to pay; in complaints usually a charged-off or delinquent account now held by a collector.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: An account placed with or sold to a collection agency after default; appears as a collection tradeline on credit reports.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Debt validation (FDCPA 809, 15 U.S.C. 1692g): the collector must send a notice of the debt, and on a timely dispute must provide verification before resuming collection.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A consumer's formal challenge to the accuracy of a reported item or a debt, sent to the CRA, the furnisher or the collector.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Fair Credit Reporting Act: the federal law governing credit reports, permissible purpose, accuracy and dispute rights.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Use of a person's identifying information to open or use accounts without authorization; triggers FCRA blocking and fraud-alert rights.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Records of who pulled a credit report; 'hard' inquiries from credit applications can lower a score, 'soft' ones do not.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: FCRA 605B block: on receipt of an identity theft report, a CRA must block the resulting items, generally within four business days.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: FCRA section 605B (15 U.S.C. 1681c-2), the identity-theft blocking provision, often cited by section number in template letters.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: On-time payment history, the largest component of common credit scores; complaints allege accurate on-time history was misreported.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Identifier of a tradeline; redacted in CFPB narratives, used by consumers to point to the specific disputed account.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: FCRA 604 (15 U.S.C. 1681b) permissible purpose: a CRA may furnish a report on the consumer's written instructions or another listed purpose; complaints allege reports were pulled without it.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Amount currently owed on an account (or available in a deposit account).
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Closed-end credit repaid in installments (auto, personal, student, mortgage), as opposed to revolving credit such as cards.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: In FCRA disputes, the CRA's confirmation with the furnisher that an item is accurate; consumers may request the method of verification (15 U.S.C. 1681i(a)(7)).
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Colloquial name for the three nationwide CRAs (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion).
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A loan secured by real property; the lender can foreclose if the borrower defaults.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Closed-end credit products; in this topic mainly student, auto (vehicle) and payday/personal loans repaid in installments.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Money in a deposit account. Banks may place holds on deposited funds; Regulation CC (12 CFR 229) sets the maximum hold periods.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A paper draft on a deposit account; complaints concern holds, returned or fraudulent checks, and check-cashing delays.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A transaction paid when the account balance is too low, usually with a fee. Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.17) banks need opt-in before charging overdraft fees on ATM and one-time debit card transactions.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: A consumer's error or fraud claim on an electronic transfer. Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.11) the bank must investigate, generally within 10 business days, or within 45 days if it provisionally credits the account.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Unauthorized use; for credit cards, TILA (15 U.S.C. 1643) caps the cardholder's liability for unauthorized charges at $50.
definition_source: general domain knowledge, not derived from the data

definition: Transactions posted to a card account; disputed charges go through the issuer's billing-error (Fair Credit Billing Act) or chargeback process.
